quests.instruction: On a stormy night, a volunteer helps a lost hiker using a map, a radio, a rope, and a first-aid kit, and works with a team. Which job's skills match best?
quests.hint: Think about navigation, safety gear, and teamwork combined.
quests.explanation: Rescue work combines map reading, communication, climbing gear, and first aid. Forecasters study weather, and camp cooks prepare meals.
quests.funFact: Mountain rescue teams often include volunteers who train regularly together.

quests.instruction: A small town's only bridge closes after a storm. Which sequence of actions is wisest?
options: Plan repairs, ignore warnings, check safety later
Warn nobody, reopen it, check safety afterward
Check safety, warn the public, plan repairs
quests.correctAnswer: Check safety, warn the public, plan repairs
quests.hint: Think about protecting people before anything else.
quests.explanation: Safety checks come first, then people must be told, and repairs can be planned with accurate information.
quests.funFact: Engineers often use signs and barriers to keep people away from damaged structures.

quests.instruction: A farmer, a chef, and a delivery driver each help get fresh soup to a table. Which order follows the food on its journey?
quests.hint: Think about growing, moving, then cooking.
quests.explanation: Vegetables are grown by a farmer, delivered to the kitchen, and then cooked by the chef.
quests.funFact: Many foods pass through several workers before they reach a kitchen.

quests.instruction: A hospital uses a doctor, a nurse, and a lab technician for one patient. Why does teamwork help?
options: It lets one person do all of the work
Each person adds a different skill
It makes the hospital building much quieter
quests.correctAnswer: Each person adds a different skill
quests.hint: Think about different skills joining together.
quests.explanation: Doctors, nurses, and lab staff each bring different training, so the patient gets better care together.
quests.funFact: Hospitals often hold short team meetings to share information about patients.

quests.instruction: Why do astronauts train with engineers and doctors on the ground?
options: Missions need technical and health skills
Doctors build the rocket engines for launch
quests.correctAnswer: Missions need technical and health skills
quests.hint: Think about machines and bodies in space.
quests.explanation: Space missions depend on machines working and people staying healthy, so both kinds of experts help.
quests.funFact: Mission control teams on the ground follow a spacecraft and support its crew.

quests.instruction: A cook washes hands, uses clean tools, and keeps raw meat apart from other food. Which value is this?
quests.hint: Think about preventing illness from germs.
quests.explanation: These habits reduce the spread of germs, which is the heart of food safety.
quests.funFact: Many kitchens use different colored chopping boards to keep foods apart.

quests.instruction: An airport's baggage belt jams during a busy morning. Which two workers most likely work together to fix it?
quests.hint: Think about who moves bags and who repairs machines.
quests.explanation: Handlers know how bags flow, and maintenance engineers repair the machine.
quests.funFact: Large airports can move many thousands of bags in a day.

quests.instruction: A museum wants to show an ancient pot to children safely. Which pair of jobs should plan the display?
quests.hint: Think about caring for objects and arranging how people see them.
quests.explanation: Curators know how to look after objects, and exhibit designers plan how visitors view them safely.
quests.funFact: Museums often use special lighting because strong light can harm old objects.

quests.instruction: A scientist wants to be sure a result is real. What should she do?
options: Repeat the test and share the method
Run it once and announce it
Hide the method from other people
quests.correctAnswer: Repeat the test and share the method
quests.hint: Think about proving something more than once.
quests.explanation: Repeating a test and sharing how it was done lets others check the result.
quests.funFact: Scientists often have their work reviewed by other experts before it is published.

quests.instruction: A morning radio show has a host who speaks, a producer who plans, and an expert at the mixing desk. Who controls the volume and quality of the audio?
quests.hint: Think about the person at the mixing desk.
quests.explanation: Audio technicians balance microphones and music so the audio is clear. Producers plan shows, and hosts speak on air.
quests.funFact: A mixing desk lets audio technicians adjust many audio signals at once.

quests.instruction: A film set needs one person to decide what the camera sees and another to guide the actors' performances. Who does each job?
quests.hint: Think about the camera expert and the person guiding the story.
quests.explanation: The cinematographer manages the camera and lighting, and the director guides the acting and storytelling.
quests.funFact: Many films are shot out of order and put together later by an editor.

quests.instruction: A new apartment block needs power, water, and safety checks before families move in. Which team covers all three?
quests.hint: Think about wires, pipes, and checking everything.
quests.explanation: Electricians handle wiring, plumbers handle water, and inspectors check safety.
quests.funFact: New buildings are usually inspected before people are allowed to live in them.

quests.instruction: A river city plans a new park that must also hold floodwater. Which is the best plan?
options: Pave the whole area to keep it dry
Design a park that can hold water
Build new houses where the river rises
quests.correctAnswer: Design a park that can hold water
quests.hint: Think about spaces with more than one purpose.
quests.explanation: A park designed for floods can hold extra water safely and still be enjoyed on dry days.
quests.funFact: Some cities build parks with low areas meant to hold floodwater.

quests.instruction: A school wants to cut food waste in its cafeteria. Which step shows good problem-solving?
options: Remove all the bins from the cafeteria
Guess a change and never check it
Measure waste, test a change, review
quests.correctAnswer: Measure waste, test a change, review
quests.hint: Think about learning from what happens.
quests.explanation: Measuring, testing, and reviewing show whether a change actually helps.
quests.funFact: Weighing food waste each day can show which meals are left uneaten.

quests.instruction: A wildlife team wants to protect the fish in a river. Which pair of tasks work together best?
options: Count the fish and keep water clean
Count the fish and add more litter
Ignore the fish and repair the roads
quests.correctAnswer: Count the fish and keep water clean
quests.hint: Think about learning how many there are and protecting where they live.
quests.explanation: Counting shows how fish are doing, and clean water helps them survive.
quests.funFact: Scientists sometimes use nets or underwater cameras to count river fish.

quests.instruction: Maya enjoys fixing things, solving puzzles, and helping people. Which group of jobs might suit her?
options: Referee, tour guide, or stage actor
quests.hint: Look for jobs that fix problems for others.
quests.explanation: Mechanics, IT experts, and plumbers all solve technical problems that help people.
quests.funFact: People of any background can train for technical careers.

quests.instruction: Omar loves animals, science, and being outdoors. Which choice fits all three?
quests.hint: Think about studying animals in nature.
quests.explanation: Wildlife biologists study animals, use science, and often work outdoors.
quests.funFact: Biologists sometimes track animals using small devices that record where they travel.

quests.instruction: Priya enjoys teaching, art, and working with groups. Which choice fits best?
quests.hint: Think about sharing creativity with learners.
quests.explanation: Art teachers share creative skills with classes. The other jobs do not combine all three.
quests.funFact: Art classes often let students try many materials, like clay and paint.

quests.instruction: A job changes quickly as technology improves. What is the best way to keep up?
quests.hint: Think about growing with the job.
quests.explanation: Learning new skills helps workers use new tools well and adapt to change.
quests.funFact: Many workers take short courses during their careers to learn new methods.

quests.instruction: A shop worker, a bus driver, and a nurse all serve the public. What is most important for all three?
quests.hint: Think about how people want to be treated.
quests.explanation: People depend on workers who are on time, careful, and polite.
quests.funFact: Many customer service jobs include training on listening and kindness.

quests.instruction: Two workers disagree about how to fix a problem. What is the most professional response?
options: Listen, compare, and test the best idea
quests.correctAnswer: Listen, compare, and test the best idea
quests.hint: Think about how teams make good decisions.
quests.explanation: Listening and testing ideas helps teams pick what works best.
quests.funFact: Engineers and scientists often compare several ideas before choosing one.

quests.instruction: A town plans a new hospital. Which three groups should be consulted first?
options: Nurses, pastry bakers, and golf players
quests.hint: Think about people who will use or run the hospital.
quests.explanation: Doctors and nurses know the work, and residents know what the community needs.
quests.funFact: Planners often hold public meetings so residents can share ideas.

quests.instruction: A power cut hits a city at night. Which workers deal with it first?
quests.hint: Think about restoring electricity and keeping people safe.
quests.explanation: Power engineers restore electricity, and emergency services help anyone in danger.
quests.funFact: Power companies often have crews on call for outages.

quests.instruction: An engineer says a design is unsafe, but the client wants to open early. What should the engineer do?
options: Approve it to avoid any argument today
Explain the risk and refuse to sign off
Stay silent and hope that nothing goes wrong
quests.correctAnswer: Explain the risk and refuse to sign off
quests.hint: Think about safety before schedules.
quests.explanation: Engineers protect people by speaking up when something is unsafe, even if it causes delay.
quests.funFact: Many engineering groups have codes of conduct that put public safety first.

quests.instruction: A baker, a pilot, and a teacher each prepare before work. Which match fits?
options: Baker checks the plane, pilot plans lessons, teacher checks ovens
Baker plans lessons, pilot checks ovens, teacher checks the plane
Baker checks ovens, pilot checks the plane, teacher plans lessons
quests.correctAnswer: Baker checks ovens, pilot checks the plane, teacher plans lessons
quests.hint: Match each worker with their own tools.
quests.explanation: Each worker prepares with what their job needs: ovens, aircraft, and lessons.
quests.funFact: Preparing before the work starts saves time and prevents errors.

quests.instruction: Which skill is helpful in almost every job?
options: Running very fast over long distances
quests.hint: Think about how teams share information.
quests.explanation: Clear communication helps workers cooperate and avoid mistakes.
quests.funFact: Many jobs use checklists and handovers to pass on information.

quests.instruction: Which statement about jobs is most accurate?
options: Anyone can explore jobs by learning skills
Only a few chosen people can ever do certain jobs
Jobs stay the same for hundreds of years
quests.correctAnswer: Anyone can explore jobs by learning skills
quests.hint: Think about learning and change.
quests.explanation: People can build skills and try different careers, and jobs themselves change as the world changes.
quests.funFact: Many jobs people do today did not exist a hundred years ago.

quests.instruction: A storm damages a community. Which team best shows many jobs working together?
options: Only one rescuer working all alone in the dark
A doctor working without a team
quests.hint: Think about many skills helping at once.
quests.explanation: Rescuers find people, doctors help the injured, engineers make places safe, and volunteers lend a hand.
quests.funFact: After storms, communities often rely on neighbors as well as professionals.

quests.instruction: After learning about so many professions, which is the best conclusion?
options: One single job is the best for everyone
Every job matters, and skills can grow
Only famous jobs are worth doing
quests.correctAnswer: Every job matters, and skills can grow
quests.hint: Think about everyone's role in a community.
quests.explanation: Communities depend on many kinds of work, and people can build new skills over time.
quests.funFact: Even small teams can need many different skills to finish a project.

quests.instruction: Which choice shows real understanding of any profession?
options: Knowing only the name of the job
Knowing what workers do, use, and why
quests.correctAnswer: Knowing what workers do, use, and why
quests.hint: Think about purpose, tools, and the people helped.
quests.explanation: Understanding a job means knowing the tasks, the tools, and how it helps others.
quests.funFact: Asking workers about their day is a good way to learn what a job is really like.
